# Hosea Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 332v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/HOS_012_page_001.jpg

---

**12:1** Efrayim feeds [ro'eh] on-wind [ruach] and-pursues [verodef] the-east-wind [qadim] all the-day [kol ha-yom]; lies [kazav] and-desolation [va-shod] he-multiplies [yarbeh]; and-a-covenant [berit] with-Ashur [Assyria] they-make [yikhrot], and-oil [shemen] to-Mitsrayim is-carried [yuval].

**12:3** In-the-womb [ba-beten] he-took-by-the-heel [aqav] his-brother [achiv], and-in-his-manhood [be-ono] he-strove [sarah] with-God [elohim].

**12:6** And-you, to-your-God [be-elohekha] you-will-return [tashuv]; loyalty [chesed] and-justice [mishpat] keep [shemor], and-wait [veqaveh] for-your-God continually [tamid].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "feeds on wind":** Ephraim's foreign policy — chasing alliances with Assyria and Egypt simultaneously — is like trying to eat the wind. The "east wind" (*qadim*) is the scorching desert wind that destroys crops — the very alliances they pursue will destroy them.

**v.3 — "he took by the heel":** A reference to Jacob's birth (Genesis 25:26). Hosea retells Jacob's story to mirror Israel's — heel-grabbing, wrestling, deception — establishing that the pattern of struggle with God is ancient.

*— EMET*
